displayTitle: A lattice problem acquired new extremizers—and a life in phase space
discipline: Convex geometry, functional analysis and symplectic geometry

scope.note: Three OpenAI manuscripts claim the symmetric and general geometric Mahler inequalities in all dimensions with geometric equality cases, their even and general functional inequalities, and Gromov width 4 for symmetric polar products. Functional equality classifications are not claimed.

originalQuestion: How small can the volume of a convex body times the volume of its polar be? Mahler's polygon paper treats planar minima, with parallelograms in the symmetric class and triangles in the general class. His 1939 transference paper explicitly conjectures the symmetric higher-dimensional lower bound 4ⁿ/n!, attained by a parallelotope and its polar cross-polytope.
modernQuestion: For origin-symmetric K in Rⁿ, is |K||K°| at least 4ⁿ/n!, with equality exactly for linear images of Hanner polytopes? For arbitrary K, after centering at its Santaló point s(K), is |K||(K−s(K))°| at least (n+1)ⁿ⁺¹/(n!)², with equality exactly for simplices? Related functional questions replace polarity by the Fenchel–Legendre transform. A stronger symplectic question asks whether int(K)×int(K°) has Gromov width 4.
questionDifference: The family comprises several statements that should not be collapsed into Mahler's original symmetric inequality. OpenAI's symmetric manuscript claims the sharp bound and the complete Hanner equality classification for every n≥1; its general manuscript separately claims the simplex bound and equality, with no symmetry or boundary regularity assumption. The functional conclusions are (∫e⁻φ)(∫e⁻φ*)≥4ⁿ when φ is even, and ≥eⁿ in general, for proper lower-semicontinuous convex φ with positive finite first integral; the second integral may be infinite. These are inequalities, without full functional equality classifications. The width manuscript claims c_G(int K×int K°)=4 for every symmetric K and n≥2, specifically embeddings of every ball of capacity c<4; it does not require an embedding at c=4 or classify geometric equality. The 2014 computation of Hofer–Zehnder capacity 4 is a different invariant and did not already prove this width statement.

conceptualOrigins.label: Polarity and Minkowski's geometry of numbers, preceding Mahler's 1930s work

firstFormulation.label: 1938–1939: planar minima and a printed symmetric conjecture

attribution: Mahler's name fits the core volume-product question, but the modern equality candidates and functional and symplectic versions were developed by others. In particular, Hanner's 1956 bodies arose in a problem about intersections of translates. Classification: gradual crystallization with unexpected connections. The first explicit symmetric all-dimensional formulation located is Mahler's transference paper, p. 96; no corresponding first-priority claim is made here for the general all-dimensional conjecture.

uncertainty: The polygon paper is dated August 1938 internally and cited as 1938 in the bibliography, while the collected archive groups it under 1939 and other accounts use 1939. The narrative preserves the range. Its approximation argument leaves equality for arbitrary planar convex regions unsettled; later equality work should not be credited wholesale to that paper. This batch has not established the first printed all-dimensional nonsymmetric conjecture or first formulation of the full Hanner equality conjecture. The manuscript-cited January 2026 width question by Alejandro Vicente could not be retrieved independently. OpenAI's proofs are not reviewed here.

events.title: Dual convex bodies help transfer lattice estimates
events.description: Mahler's introduction starts from Khintchine's transference principle, relating approximation problems, and seeks a convex-geometric generalization using Minkowski's lattice theorems. The body and its polar provide the dual pair; their volume product is invariant under linear coordinate changes.
events.relationNote: The motivating setting is lattice geometry; the extremal-volume question becomes a problem in its own right.

events.title: Planar theorems accompany a higher-dimensional conjecture
events.description: Mahler's polygon paper proves planar minima with triangle and parallelogram equality among polygons. His transference paper explicitly proposes 4ⁿ/n! as the symmetric sharp lower bound, exhibiting parallelotopes and their polar cross-polytopes.
events.relationNote: Proved planar cases and conjectured higher-dimensional behavior coexist from the outset.
events.uncertainty: The polygon paper's final paragraph extends inequalities by approximation but leaves general-region equality undecided. Its publication year varies between bibliographic accounts.

events.title: Future extremizers arise from intersections of translates
events.description: Hanner studies convex bodies with special intersection properties. His recursively constructed family mixes Cartesian products and convex-hull sums of intervals, going beyond cubes and cross-polytopes; it later becomes central to the symmetric equality question.
events.relationNote: A separate structural problem supplies the modern candidate equality family; this is not presented as Mahler's original list.

events.title: The correct exponential scale is proved
events.description: Bourgain and Milman obtain |K||K°|≥cⁿ|B₂ⁿ|² for symmetric convex bodies, with c>0 independent of dimension. This reverse Santaló theorem establishes an exponential-order lower bound, without reaching the conjectured sharp constant.
events.relationNote: Asymptotic progress is substantial even though it does not classify minimizers.

events.title: Convex duality reaches functions and symplectic billiards
events.description: Fradelizi–Meyer formulate functional lower inequalities for log-concave functions and their Legendre duals. Artstein-Avidan–Karasev–Ostrover then show in 2013–2014 that a symplectic volume–capacity conjecture would imply symmetric Mahler, computing Hofer–Zehnder capacity 4 for K×K° via billiards.
events.relationNote: Two distinct branches introduce new objects and stronger questions.
events.uncertainty: The general Viterbo volume–capacity conjecture was subsequently disproved; its conditional historical implication should not be read as a successful general proof route.

events.title: The symmetric three-dimensional problem is settled
events.description: Iriyeh and Shibata prove the sharp lower bound in dimension three and identify equality as the cube or octahedron up to an invertible linear map.
events.relationNote: A complete fixed-dimensional result includes equality, rather than only an improved universal estimate.

events.title: Three manuscripts claim several related endpoints
events.description: OpenAI claims both geometric inequalities in every dimension, with Hanner and simplex equality respectively; functional bounds 4ⁿ for even potentials and eⁿ generally; and Gromov width 4 for symmetric polar products. The width theorem supplies ball embeddings at every capacity below 4 and independently implies the symmetric volume inequality.
events.relationNote: The geometric equality, functional inequality and symplectic-width statements have different scopes.
events.uncertainty: No independent proof review. Functional equality classifications and a general Viterbo theorem are not claimed.
